correctness.rationale: The path obstruction, exact star-component selection cases, separate unused-coordinate factors and coefficient necessity/sufficiency were reconstructed for all valid integer parameters. In the padded range every positive trace can be extended using r and s unused coordinates, proving the star-forest quota criterion. The labeled exponential formula and extremal two-star counting establish all stated coefficients and VC bounds. A C++17 enumeration of actual uniform-product traces and a separate Python polynomial-inventory implementation agreed; independent active-vertex enumeration reproduced stable coefficients. Computational checks are finite corroboration, not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The two closest published full statements were read. The unrestricted Cartesian-rectangle result covers only the star-forest prerequisite and unrestricted coefficient enumerator; the exact-two-by-two result covers a special case and is credited. Neither yields exact all-quota finite feasibility, the fixed-rank padded generating polynomial, or the rs binomial extremal count for r,s>=3. The 2021 primary P4-free paper studies induced-path-free graph partition/cover rather than shattering of fixed-cardinality product concepts. Historical priority is not guaranteed.
residual_risks: The existing unrestricted rectangle theorem supplies the main path obstruction; some consequences may have been independently derived elsewhere under uniform biclique or rank-one binary matrix terminology.
The first 2020 seminar was publicly advertised but does not provide a manuscript of its exact presentation.
The 2023 biclique paper was inspected only at abstract level; no definitive exclusion of its full text is asserted.

value.rationale: The exact-row/exact-column constraint is natural in sparse rectangle and binary rank-one classification. The all-parameter inventory criterion is a componentwise exact decision method that distinguishes finite-board obstructions invisible to unrestricted star forests. The padded-range polynomial determines every support count, and the maximum-support formula for r,s>=3 gives a natural extremal classification with applications to shattering-complex face enumeration. It is not merely a recomputation of a single known dimension.
